explanation: Count occurrences with Counter, then ask most_common(k) for the k greatest frequencies. It selects by frequency using a bounded heap when k is smaller than the number of distinct values, with special cases for one result or all results.
timeComplexity: O(n + u log(k+1)) expected time for n inputs and u distinct values. Counter scans n values; selecting k frequencies scans u records and maintains at most k heap entries, then orders the selected entries. When k=u, sorting all u records has the same bound.
spaceComplexity: O(u+k) space for the Counter and selection/output records.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 Python algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: Counter records exactly each value’s multiplicity. most_common(k) retains the k greatest counts; a bounded min-heap discards only a count no larger than those it retains. The strict selection boundary fixes membership even though output ordering within a frequency tie is unrestricted.
walkthrough: For [4,4,4,7,7,9] and k=2, frequencies are 4→3,7→2,9→1. Descending frequency order is 4,7,9, so the top two values are [4,7], in either accepted order.
edgeCases: k may equal the number of distinct values.
The kth frequency must exceed the next frequency when another value exists.
